body.statement: For \(V=\{1,2,3,4\}\) with binary \(\{-1,+1\}\) states, the tuple \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\). The table \(p_{\star}\) has exactly the elementary CIs \(1\perp2\), \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\), \(3\perp4\), and \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\). Among all \(543\) labelled DAGs, exactly \(50\) are I-maps, and the unique four-edge minima are \(D_A\) and \(D_B\), which lie in distinct MECs. Their probabilities for \(Y_3=+1\) under \(do(Y_1=+1)\) are \(13/20\) and \(1/2\), respectively.
body.justification: The finite instance proves that the target family is nonvacuous beyond one Markov equivalence class.
body.gap: The examples in Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo motivate tied sparsest outputs but do not provide this binary rational exact-oracle enumeration certificate.
body.consumer: Implementers obtain a unit test whose graph counts, oracle bits, and intervention gap are all checkable by exact arithmetic.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(t=t_\star=1/3\).  Summing the unnormalised numerator first over \(s_3\) and then over \(s_4\) gives
\[
 \sum_{s_3=\pm1}(1+ts_1s_3)(1+ts_2s_3)=2(1+t^2s_1s_2),
\]
\[
 \sum_{s_4=\pm1}(1+ts_1s_4)(1-ts_2s_4)=2(1-t^2s_1s_2).
\]
Their product is \(4(1-t^4)\), independently of \((s_1,s_2)\).  Summing over the four choices of \((s_1,s_2)\) therefore gives \(16(1-t^4)=1280/81\), proving normalization.  All four factors lie in \(\{2/3,4/3\}\), so every cell is positive.  In lexicographic \((-1,+1)\) order the sixteen probabilities are
\[
 \frac1{40}(4,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,4).
\]
Thus the table is rational, sums to one, and has minimum cell \(1/40\).

The preceding two summations show \(p_\star(s_1,s_2)=1/4\), hence \(1\perp2\).  Interchanging \((s_1,s_2)\) and \((s_3,s_4)\) gives \(p_\star(s_3,s_4)=1/4\), hence \(3\perp4\).  Conditional on \((s_1,s_2)\), the numerator is a product of one function of \(s_3\) and one function of \(s_4\); hence \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\).  Conditional on \((s_3,s_4)\), it is similarly a product of one function of \(s_1\) and one function of \(s_2\); hence \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\).

For completeness, define the elementary conditional-independence minor
\[
 \Delta_{ij\mid C}(a,b,c)
 =p(a,b,c)p(c)-p(a,c)p(b,c).
\]
Direct summation of the displayed integer table gives the following nonzero witness for every one of the other twenty elementary statements.  In every row \(a=b=-1\), and all displayed coordinates of \(c\) equal \(-1\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c@{\qquad}c|c|c}
(i,j)&C&\Delta&(i,j)&C&\Delta\\ \hline
(1,2)&\{3\}&-9/1600 &(1,2)&\{4\}&9/1600\\
(1,3)&\varnothing&3/40 &(1,3)&\{2\}&3/160\\
(1,3)&\{4\}&3/160 &(1,3)&\{2,4\}&3/1600\\
(1,4)&\varnothing&3/40 &(1,4)&\{2\}&3/160\\
(1,4)&\{3\}&3/160 &(1,4)&\{2,3\}&3/400\\
(2,3)&\varnothing&3/40 &(2,3)&\{1\}&3/160\\
(2,3)&\{4\}&3/160 &(2,3)&\{1,4\}&3/400\\
(2,4)&\varnothing&-3/40 &(2,4)&\{1\}&-3/160\\
(2,4)&\{3\}&-3/160 &(2,4)&\{1,3\}&-3/400\\
(3,4)&\{1\}&-9/1600 &(3,4)&\{2\}&9/1600
\end{array}
\]
The four factorizations already proved make all their minors zero, while the table makes at least one minor nonzero for each remaining statement.  Hence these are exactly the elementary conditional independences.

It remains to verify the finite graph certificate.  Every labelled four-node DAG is generated by choosing a permutation, choosing a subset of its six forward pairs, and deduplicating edge sets.  Inclusion--exclusion on the nonempty set of sources gives the recurrence
\[
 a_q=\sum_{k=1}^q(-1)^{k+1}{q\choose k}2^{k(q-k)}a_{q-k},
 \qquad a_0=1,
\]
and hence \((a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=(1,1,3,25,543)\).  For each of these \(543\) edge sets, enumerate all disjoint triples of node subsets, test d-separation by active paths, and, whenever d-separation holds, test every corresponding table minor by integer cross-multiplication.  Grouping the resulting exact Boolean certificate by edge count gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
\text{edge count}&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{all DAGs}&1&12&60&152&186&108&24\\
\text{I-maps}&0&0&0&0&2&24&24
\end{array}
\]
and the two four-edge I-maps have edge sets
\[
 \{1\to3,1\to4,2\to3,2\to4\},\qquad
 \{3\to1,3\to2,4\to1,4\to2\}.
\]
This enumeration is checkable solely by the displayed integer table, finite active-path tests, and integer equalities.  As a separate lower-bound check, the determinant table shows that each of the four cross pairs \(\{1,3\},\{1,4\},\{2,3\},\{2,4\}\) is inseparable by every subset of the other two vertices.  If one of these pairs were nonadjacent in an I-map DAG, take the later vertex in a topological order; its local Markov statement given its parents would separate that pair, contradicting the corresponding nonzero minor.  Thus every I-map has at least four edges, confirming minimality independently of the count.  The two DAGs are not Markov equivalent: \(D_A\) d-separates \(1\) and \(2\), whereas \(D_B\) does not, and \(D_B\) d-separates \(3\) and \(4\), whereas \(D_A\) does not.

Both displayed DAG factorizations follow from the four proved conditional independences.  Under \(D_A\), truncation at \(s_1=+1\) and summation over \(s_2,s_4\) give
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)
 =\sum_{s_2}p_\star(s_2)p_\star(s_3=+1\mid s_1=+1,s_2)
 =p_\star(s_3=+1\mid s_1=+1),
\]
where the second equality uses \(1\perp2\).  Direct sign summation gives uniform one-variable marginals and
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_t}[s_1s_3]
 =\frac{t(1-t^2)}{1-t^4}=\frac{t}{1+t^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)=\frac12+\frac{t}{2(1+t^2)}=\frac{13}{20}.
\]
Under \(D_B\), node \(3\) is an unmanipulated root; deleting the factor for intervened node \(1\) and summing the remaining conditional factors gives
\[
 T_{D_B,+1}(p_\star)=p_\star(s_3=+1)=\frac12.
\]
Thus the supplied empty background set, graph family, query, and rational table pass every check in \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), and all assertions follow.
